title: City's appeal plan revealed

segments.say: Manchester City have until Friday to appeal the biggest verdict in Premier League history.
And today, we found out exactly how they plan to fight it.
Quick recap. On Tuesday, an independent commission found City broke Premier League rules on 114 of the 115 charges.
The biggest finding? £830m of the owner's money, dressed up as sponsorship income, between 2009 and 2018.

visual.label: owner funding the commission says was disguised as sponsorship

segments.say: Sky Sports reports City will argue that money came from the Abu Dhabi government, not from owner Sheikh Mansour.
Why does that matter? Because sponsorship backed by a government is allowed under the rules.
So what happens next? City lodge the appeal by Friday. A brand new appeal board hears it. And the punishment? Still not decided.
City deny any wrongdoing, and say the decision contains clear errors.

visual.text: Clear material errors, of law, principle and fact

segments.say: So here's the question. A fine, a points deduction, or something bigger? Tell me in the comments, and follow for tomorrow's update.

caption: Man City 115 charges update, Day 3: City have until Friday to appeal, and Sky Sports reports they'll argue the £830m came from the Abu Dhabi government, not the owner. Punishment not decided yet. Sources: Premier League decision 29/09, Sky Sports, Inside World Football. AI voiceover.
